title: How to Get Urine Smell Out of a Mattress

seo.title: How to Get Urine Smell Out of a Mattress
seo.meta_description: To remove urine odor from a mattress, absorb moisture, use a small amount of compatible cleaner, and dry completely. Deep foam contamination changes the problem.
seo.search_intent: Remove urine residue and odor from a mattress without soaking it, mixing chemicals, or trapping moisture inside the fill.

excerpt: Cleaning urine from a mattress is not a matter of flooding the spot. The more liquid you add, the harder it becomes to dry the internal layers and prevent musty odor.
content_html:
For a fresh accident, absorb as much as possible before cleaning. Press with clean towels and change them as they become wet; do not scrub the liquid sideways.

Strip the bed and separate damp layers

Launder sheets and the mattress protector according to their labels. If moisture reached a platform or foundation, separate the surfaces so dampness is not trapped between them.

Use a small amount of cleaner

An enzyme cleaner labeled for compatible textiles can help break down organic residue. Follow its contact time and test for color or finish change. Do not saturate the mattress.

Extract moisture again

Press with dry towels until they pick up little moisture. Use a wet vacuum only if it is suitable for the task and the mattress manufacturer permits that method.

Dry completely before remaking the bed

Ventilate, use gentle air movement, and leave the mattress uncovered. Do not add bedding while the interior still feels cool or damp.

Old urine may have reached the foam

If odor returns in humid weather or after several surface treatments, residue may be deeper than household cleaning can reach. Repeatedly wetting the top can make drying harder; professional cleaning or replacement may be more realistic.

Never combine chlorine bleach with ammonia, acids, or other cleaners. Moisture control is as important here as odor treatment.

faq.question: Should I soak the mattress so cleaner reaches deep into it?
faq.answer: No. Excess liquid is difficult to remove from internal layers and can create a moisture problem.

faq.question: Do enzyme cleaners help?
faq.answer: They can help with organic residue when they are compatible with the mattress fabric and used as directed.

faq.question: What if the smell keeps coming back?
faq.answer: The contamination may be deep in the fill. Avoid repeated soaking and consider professional cleaning or replacement.
